build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: An alchemy map shows a 2D space with ingredient zones. The player navigates a cursor from the center outward, passing through zones that add properties to the brew. The path taken determines the potion type. Score 0 if no alchemy map navigation exists.

Reaching a recipe zone on the alchemy map and bottling creates a specific potion type (healing, fire resistance, invisibility, etc.). At least 5 distinct potion types are discoverable. Score 0 if no recipe/bottling system exists.

Customers arrive with orders showing desired potion types via icons. Fulfilling an order earns gold and reputation. Failing or ignoring orders loses reputation. Score 0 if no customer order system exists.

A reputation system tracks shop standing. High reputation unlocks rarer ingredients and harder customers. Losing all reputation ends the run. Reputation is visible and changes with each fulfilled or failed order. Score 0 if no reputation system exists.

Gold earned from sales buys map reveals (uncovering hidden ingredient zones), better tools (faster cursor, wider paths), and ingredient restocks. The economy creates meaningful spending decisions. Score 0 if no shop or spending exists.

The alchemy map is partially hidden and revealed through exploration or purchases. At least 5 distinct ingredient zones exist with different visual identities and effects on the brew. Score 0 if the map is fully visible from the start or has fewer than 4 zones.

Customer variety increases over days — early customers want simple potions, later customers want rare or complex recipes. At least 3 tiers of customer difficulty exist. Score 0 if all customers want the same thing.

Recipe discovery is experimental — the player must explore the alchemy map to find where recipe zones are located. A recipe book records discovered recipes for future reference. Score 0 if all recipes are known from the start.

Each run generates a new alchemy map layout — ingredient zones are in different positions, requiring re-discovery of recipe paths. No two runs have identical maps. Score 0 if the map is always the same.
A run-end evaluation shows days survived, reputation earned, gold total, recipes discovered, and orders fulfilled. The evaluation reflects actual performance. Score 0 if no results exist.
A styled title screen shows bubbling cauldrons and potion bottles with the game name. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> shop day -> customer orders -> alchemy brewing -> delivery -> next day without restarting. Score 0 if transitions are missing.

During brewing, the alchemy map shows the cursor position, explored/unexplored areas, ingredient zones, and recipe targets. Customer orders and reputation are visible. Score 0 if no map visualization exists.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: ingredient zones, recipe targets, cursor path, customers, and potion types are all clearly distinguishable. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, alchemy map, shop, customers, and UI — a consistent medieval alchemy aesthetic with warm palette. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The alchemy map uses illustrated ingredient art, potion bottles have distinct visual designs, and customers have character sprites — not plain shapes or text. Score 0 if map elements are colored dots.

HUD and UI chrome: reputation bar, gold counter, recipe book, customer panels, and shop interface use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: the cursor leaves a trail on the alchemy map, bottling has a bubbling animation, customers react visually to fulfilled/failed orders, and reputation changes have visual flair. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
